chunks: From him, from Abu Al-Qasim Al-Kufi, from the one who narrated it, from Muhammad ibn Al-Walid Al-Kirmani, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second, 'What do you say regarding musk?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) ordered for musk to be made for him in a container for seven hundred dirhams. So Al-Fadl ibn Sahl wrote to him, informing him that the people were criticizing that. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'O Fadl! Do you not know that Yusuf (peace be upon him), and he was a prophet, used to wear brocade buttoned with gold, and would sit upon chairs of gold, and that did not reduce anything from his wisdom?' He (the narrator) said, 'So he ordered for a Ghaliya to be made for him for four thousand dirhams.'

key_terms.بَان: A container or vessel for holding perfume
key_terms.غَالِيَةٌ: A specific type of high-quality perfume or scent
key_terms.مِسْك: Musk, a type of expensive perfume

ai.seo_question: Does wearing expensive perfume or luxury items contradict piety in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) justifies the use of high-quality musk by referencing a precedent set by his father, Imam Al-Baqir, who commissioned an expensive batch despite criticism from the Abbasid vizier Al-Fadl ibn Sahl. By citing Prophet Yusuf’s attire of brocade and gold, the Imam establishes that material luxury does not inherently detract from spiritual wisdom or prophetic status, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the permissibility of premium goods for the pious.
